reviewBoundary: These are review-ready drafts, not verified publication chapters. No machine setting, safety procedure, or material processing value may be inferred from them.

sourceSeeds.title: Plastics — Injection moulding of test specimens of thermoplastic materials — Part 1: General principles, and moulding of multipurpose and bar test specimens
sourceSeeds.scope: General injection-moulding principles, consistent process-parameter descriptions and reproducible reporting. ISO confirms the 2017 edition remains current after review in 2022.

chapters.applicability: General thermoplastic injection-moulding concepts only. Actual process windows depend on the material grade, machine, mould, part requirements and applicable site controls.

sections.title: The process in one sentence
sections.text: At its simplest, injection moulding prepares a polymer melt, pushes a controlled shot into a closed mould, lets the material form and solidify enough to handle, then opens the mould and removes the part so the cycle can begin again.

sections.title: What the process must achieve
sections.text: Getting plastic into the cavity is only the start. A production process has to make the required shape and properties repeatedly, while keeping the material, machine, mould and safety system inside their working limits.

sections.title: Why settings are not universal
sections.text: There is no set of moulding conditions that can simply be carried from one job to the next. Even standards written for reproducible test specimens recognise that the required conditions change with the material. Production parts add geometry, mould design, machine capability and quality requirements to that picture.

sections.title: How to think like a process engineer
sections.text: Start with the part result you need, then work back to the machine inputs that create it. Watch what the material and cavity are actually doing, record the conditions that matter, and when you need to learn cause and effect, make one justified change at a time.

chapters.applicability: Conceptual cycle model. Controller names, available phases and transition methods vary by machine and process.

sections.title: Prepare the next shot
sections.text: While one part is often still cooling in the mould, the plasticising unit is already preparing the next shot. The screw rotates and moves back as it builds a controlled quantity of melt. What happens here matters: material preparation and thermal history carry forward into the next injection.

sections.title: Fill the cavity
sections.text: When injection starts, the screw moves forward and melt travels through the nozzle, feed system and gate into the cavity. The machine is commanding motion while the flow path is pushing back against it. The pressure shown on the machine is useful evidence, but it is not the same thing as pressure inside the cavity.

sections.title: Transfer and pack
sections.text: Near the end of filling, the process changes from driving the flow front forward to controlling the post-fill pressure. Packing then helps compensate for material contraction while the gate and part can still respond. Where that transition belongs, and how packing should be applied, has to be established on the actual moulded system rather than copied from a generic percentage or pressure.

sections.title: Cool and eject
sections.text: The part stays in the mould until it is stiff and stable enough to be released without unacceptable distortion or damage. How long that takes is influenced by the material, part geometry, mould-temperature distribution and the way heat leaves the tool.

sections.title: Treat the cycle as an interacting system
sections.text: The controller may divide the cycle into neat stages, but the physics does not stop at those boundaries. Plasticising can happen while the part cools, and the thermal or pressure history created in one stage can change the next. When something drifts, look at the whole sequence rather than one screen value in isolation.

chapters.applicability: General injection-moulding-machine architecture. Exact guarding, drives, controls and component names depend on the machine manufacturer and configuration.

sections.title: Injection unit
sections.text: The injection unit takes in the raw material, plasticises it, meters the shot and sends the melt toward the mould. A typical reciprocating-screw machine includes a feed system, heated barrel, screw, non-return function and nozzle, although the details and control methods vary between machines.

sections.title: Clamping unit
sections.text: The clamping unit carries the mould and manages the mechanical side of the cycle: closing, clamping, opening and the motions associated with part release. Machines may be hydraulic, electric or hybrid, and the way they generate and transmit clamp force can differ considerably.

sections.title: Control and energy systems
sections.text: The controller brings together motion commands, temperatures, pressures, timing, alarms and interlocks, but it only shows part of the machine. Behind the process screen are electrical, mechanical, hydraulic, pneumatic or other energy sources, including stored energy that may remain hazardous when the machine appears stopped.

sections.title: Use the machine documentation
sections.text: For setup, guarding, isolation, maintenance, operating limits and permitted work, the machine manufacturer's instructions and the site's approved procedures are the authority. This chapter can explain the machine, but it cannot replace those instructions.

chapters.applicability: General mould-component concepts and terminology. Actual mould construction varies widely and may omit or add systems described here.

sections.title: The mould creates the part-forming space
sections.text: The core and cavity surfaces form the shape of the part, but that is only one of the mould's jobs. The tool also has to accept the melt, remove heat, open in a controlled way and release the moulding without damaging either the part or the tooling.

sections.title: Feed system
sections.text: In a conventional cold-feed system, the melt may pass through a sprue, runners and gates before it reaches the cavity. A hot runner changes how that melt is carried and controlled. In either case, the gate matters twice: it is a restriction during filling and a boundary for post-fill pressure, so its geometry and thermal condition can strongly influence the process.

sections.title: Guidance, support and ejection
sections.text: Locating, guiding and supporting components keep the mould aligned and carry the loads generated during the cycle. Once the part is ready to come out, the ejection system provides the release motion. The exact arrangement is something to identify on the real tool, not something to assume from a generic mould diagram.

sections.title: Temperature-control system
sections.text: Temperature-control circuits move heat into or out of the mould so it can reach a useful and repeatable thermal condition. Because circuit layout, flow condition and local heat load are rarely identical everywhere, two areas of the tool can sit at different surface temperatures even when the controller shows one setpoint.

chapters.applicability: Awareness only. It is not a lockout/tagout procedure, machine-specific safe system of work, guarding instruction or authorisation to enter a hazardous area.

sections.title: Safety is a system boundary
sections.text: An injection-moulding machine brings together powerful motion, hot material and surfaces, pressure, electricity and other machine-dependent energy sources. Safe work comes from the complete system: sound engineered safeguards, a machine in the correct condition, authorised procedures and people who are competent for the task.

sections.title: A stopped screen is not an isolation
sections.text: A machine that is not moving can still contain hazardous energy. A stopped cycle, an open guard or a quiet controller screen does not prove that energy has been isolated or dissipated, so none of those conditions should be treated as permission to intervene.

sections.title: Guarding and interlocks are safety functions
sections.text: Guards and interlocks are there to control real hazards, not to get in the way of production. Do not defeat or bypass them. If a safeguard prevents the job you are trying to do, use the approved machine- and site-specific method for that task instead of improvising around the protection.

sections.title: When this Book must stop
sections.text: There is a clear point where general process guidance ends. If the work involves entering a danger zone, isolating energy, maintenance, stored energy, an abnormal machine condition or uncertainty about a safeguard, stop using this Book as the procedure. Follow the machine manufacturer's instructions, the site's authorised safety system and competent supervision.
